unit: Ch 6: Deductions from Gross Total Income
note: AI-written summary of ICAI study material. Check the original for exact wording.

topics.title: General Principles of Deductions
explain: Deductions reduce Gross Total Income to arrive at taxable Total Income.
They are available only if the assessee opts out of the default tax regime u/s 202(1).
Aggregate Chapter VIII deductions cannot exceed Gross Total Income.
Deductions cannot create or increase a loss to carry forward.
No deduction is allowed against special-rate incomes like lottery or capital gains.
Part C deductions require filing return on or before the section 263(1) due date.

flow.title: Applying Chapter VIII Deductions
steps: Compute Gross Total Income across heads
Exclude special incomes like LTCG or lottery
Aggregate eligible Chapter VIII deductions
Limit deductions up to remaining Gross Total Income
Total Income becomes positive or nil

topics.example: If your GTI is ₹4,80,000 and total eligible deductions are ₹5,50,000, your allowable deduction is capped at ₹4,80,000, making taxable income nil.
remember: Total deductions cannot exceed GTI.
Return must be filed within due date for Part C profit-linked deductions.
mistakes: Claiming Chapter VIII deductions to create a net negative loss figure to carry forward.

quiz.q: A taxpayer has a Gross Total Income of ₹4,80,000 and eligible deductions of ₹5,50,000. How much deduction can be claimed?
quiz.why: Section 122(2) restricts the aggregate deductions to the gross total income.

quiz.q: What happens to Part C profit-linked deductions if the return of income is filed after the due date?
quiz.why: Section 122(5) strictly denies Part C deductions if the return is not filed by the due date.

topics.title: Deduction for Investment in Specified Assets
explain: Available only to Individuals and HUFs opting out of the default tax regime.
Covers investments like PPF, EPF, life insurance premium, tuition fees, and NSC.
Also covers principal repayment of housing loan and 5-year bank/post office term deposits.
Total deduction across all eligible instruments under section 123 is capped at ₹1,50,000.
Life insurance premium is capped at 10% of sum assured (20% for pre-1.4.2012 policies, 15% for disabled).
Tuition fee deduction is restricted to full-time education for a maximum of 2 children.

flow.title: Computation of Section 123 Deduction
steps: Check individual item limits like insurance cap
Add all qualifying investments and payments
Sum total of all eligible instruments
Compare aggregate sum with ₹1,50,000 limit
Allow lower of aggregate or ₹1,50,000

topics.example: If you pay ₹1,50,000 in PPF and ₹30,000 life insurance premium, total qualifying payment is ₹1,80,000, but allowable deduction is capped at ₹1,50,000.
remember: Overall ceiling limit is ₹1,50,000.
Tuition fee excludes development fees, coaching, and overseas colleges.
mistakes: Claiming life insurance premium paid for parents; Section 123 only covers self, spouse, and children.

quiz.q: For a life insurance policy issued on 15.05.2020 with a sum assured of ₹2,50,000, what is the maximum deductible premium under section 123?
quiz.why: For policies issued after 31.03.2012, deduction is capped at 10% of sum assured (10% of ₹2,50,000 = ₹25,000).

quiz.q: What happens if a house property acquired using loan is transferred within 5 years from end of tax year of possession?
o: Earlier deductions allowed become taxable income
50% of the loan principal is forfeited
quiz.why: Section 123 rules deem deductions allowed in earlier years as income upon breach of the 5-year lock-in.

topics.title: Deduction for Contribution to Pension Schemes
explain: Covers contributions made to notified pension schemes like NPS and APY.
Employer contribution u/s 124(1) is deductible up to 14% of salary for Government employers.
For non-Government employers, it is 10% of salary (or 14% under default tax regime).
Employer contribution deduction is available under both default and optional regimes.
Employee self-contribution allows an additional deduction up to ₹50,000 u/s 124(3).
Section 124(4) extends this ₹50,000 limit to contributions made to NPS Vatsalya for minors.

flow.title: Evaluating NPS Deductions
steps: Include employer contribution in salary income
Deduct employer contribution u/s 124(1) up to limits
Evaluate employee own contribution to NPS
Claim excess employee share under section 123

topics.example: A private employee with salary of ₹10,00,000 whose employer contributes ₹1,40,000 can deduct ₹1,40,000 under default regime (14%) or ₹1,00,000 under optional regime (10%).
remember: Salary for NPS means Basic Salary + DA forming part of retirement benefits.
Additional ₹50,000 deduction u/s 124(3) is only under optional tax regime.
mistakes: Thinking employer contribution to NPS is exempt at source without adding it to gross salary first.

quiz.q: Under the default tax regime, what is the maximum employer NPS contribution deduction for a private company employee?
quiz.why: Under section 124(1)/(2), the limit is 14% of salary for non-government employees if taxable u/s 202(1).

quiz.q: What is the maximum combined deduction limit for employee NPS u/s 124(3) and NPS Vatsalya u/s 124(4)?
quiz.why: The aggregate deduction under sections 124(3) and 124(4) cannot exceed ₹50,000.

topics.title: Deduction for Contribution to Agnipath Scheme
explain: Applies to individuals enrolled in the Agnipath Scheme subscribing to Agniveer Corpus Fund.
Individual contributes 30% of monthly package; Central Government matches the contribution.
Assessee's own contribution is deductible u/s 125(1) under the optional tax regime.
Central Government contribution is included in salary and fully deductible u/s 125(2).
Deduction u/s 125(2) is available under both default and optional tax regimes.
Maturity payments from the Agniveer Corpus Fund are entirely exempt from income tax.

flow.title: Agniveer Corpus Scheme Accounting
steps: Individual contributes 30% of package
Central Government provides equal matching contribution
Add Central Government share to gross salary
Claim deduction u/s 125(2) across both regimes
Claim own contribution u/s 125(1) if opting out

topics.example: An Agniveer receiving ₹30,000 monthly contributes ₹9,000; the Government also deposits ₹9,000. Both amounts qualify for deduction according to the selected regime.
remember: Government contribution is deductible under both default and optional tax regimes.
Receipts on completion from the fund are fully tax-exempt.
mistakes: Forgetting to include the Central Government's contribution in gross salary before claiming deduction.

quiz.q: Which deduction under section 125 is available even if the assessee pays tax under the default tax regime?
quiz.why: Section 125(2) for Central Government's contribution is allowed under the default tax regime u/s 202(1).

quiz.q: What portion of monthly Agniveer package is contributed by the individual to the Corpus Fund?
quiz.why: Each Agniveer contributes 30% of their monthly customized package.

topics.title: Deduction for Health Insurance Premium
explain: Available to Individuals and HUFs under the optional tax regime.
Covers health insurance premium, CGHS contribution, and preventive health check-up.
Basic limit is ₹25,000 for self, spouse, and dependent children (₹50,000 if senior citizen).
Additional limit is ₹25,000 for parents (₹50,000 if either parent is a senior citizen).
Preventive health check-up has an overall sub-limit of ₹5,000 (allowed in cash).
Medical expenditure up to ₹50,000 is allowed for uninsured senior citizens.

flow.title: Determining Health Insurance Deduction
steps: Compute premium and check-up for family (max ₹25,000/₹50,000)
Check preventive health check-up across family (max ₹5,000)
Compute premium and expenses for parents (max ₹25,000/₹50,000)
Verify payment mode (non-cash except check-up)
Sum both buckets for total section 126 deduction

topics.example: A 40-year-old pays ₹20,000 for his own insurance and ₹47,000 for his senior citizen father's insurance. Allowed deduction is ₹20,000 + ₹47,000 = ₹67,000.
remember: Parents need not be dependent to claim deduction for their health insurance.
Cash payment is permitted ONLY for preventive health check-up up to ₹5,000.
mistakes: Paying health insurance premium in cash; cash insurance payments are completely disallowed.

quiz.q: What is the maximum deduction allowed for preventive health check-up within the overall section 126 limits?
quiz.why: Deduction on account of preventive health check-up is capped at ₹5,000 in aggregate.

quiz.q: Ms. Pooja (38) pays ₹28,000 health insurance for her mother (66) and ₹18,000 medical expenses for her father (70, uninsured). What is the total deduction?
quiz.why: Both parents are senior citizens sharing a single limit of ₹50,000. Total spent ₹28,000 + ₹18,000 = ₹46,000, fully allowable.

topics.title: Maintenance & Medical Treatment of a Dependant Disabled
explain: Available to resident Individuals and HUFs under the optional tax regime.
Covers medical treatment, training, rehabilitation, or deposits in LIC schemes for a disabled dependant.
Dependant includes spouse, children, parents, brothers, and sisters wholly reliant on assessee.
Fixed deduction of up to ₹75,000 is allowed for ordinary disability (40% or more).
Enhanced deduction of up to ₹1,25,000 is allowed for severe disability (80% or more).
A medical certificate must be furnished with the return filed under section 263.

flow.title: Evaluating Section 127 Deduction
steps: Verify person is an eligible dependant
Ensure dependant has not claimed section 154
Determine disability percentage from medical certificate
Allow ₹75,000 for regular disability
Allow ₹1,25,000 if severe disability (80%+)

topics.example: If an individual incurs ₹40,000 on medical treatment for a dependant brother who has 85% disability, the deduction allowed is the flat severe limit of ₹1,25,000.
remember: Grandparents are NOT included in the definition of dependant.
Deduction is irrespective of the actual expenditure incurred.
mistakes: Claiming section 127 when the disabled person has already claimed section 154 on their own return.

quiz.q: Mr. X deposits ₹1,50,000 for the maintenance of his disabled grandfather. How much can he claim u/s 127?
quiz.why: Grandfather does not fall within the statutory definition of 'dependant' under section 127.

quiz.q: What is the quantum of deduction under section 127 in case of severe disability (80% or more)?
quiz.why: For severe disability (80% or more), deduction allowed is up to ₹1,25,000.

topics.title: Deduction for Medical Treatment of Specified Diseases
explain: Available to resident Individuals and HUFs under the optional tax regime.
For medical treatment of prescribed chronic or critical diseases (e.g., cancer, neurological disorders).
Deduction is actual sum paid or ₹40,000, whichever is less.
Limit increases to actual sum paid or ₹1,00,000, whichever is less, for senior citizens.
Any amount reimbursed by an employer or received from an insurance company reduces the deduction.
Must obtain a valid prescription from a prescribed medical specialist.

flow.title: Calculating Section 128 Relief
steps: Check expenditure on prescribed specified disease
Determine threshold limit (₹40,000 or ₹1,00,000)
Take lower of actual expenditure and ceiling limit
Subtract insurance or employer reimbursements
Net figure qualifies as section 128 deduction

topics.example: If ₹90,000 is spent on cancer treatment for a 65-year-old father and insurance pays ₹30,000, deduction is ₹90,000 (capped at ₹1,00,000) minus ₹30,000 = ₹60,000.
remember: Senior citizen limit is ₹1,00,000; non-senior citizen limit is ₹40,000.
Always net off insurance claim recoveries.
mistakes: Claiming the flat ceiling without reducing insurance recovery received from the insurer.

quiz.q: What is the maximum deduction under section 128 for medical treatment of a non-senior citizen?
quiz.why: Section 128 allows actual payment or ₹40,000, whichever is less, for non-senior citizens.

quiz.q: If an assessee spends ₹80,000 on specified treatment of his senior citizen mother and receives ₹50,000 from mediclaim, deduction is:
quiz.why: Deduction is min(₹80,000, ₹1,00,000) - ₹50,000 insurance recovery = ₹30,000.

topics.title: Interest on Loan for Higher Education
explain: Available to individuals paying interest out of taxable income under optional regime.
Loan must be taken from a bank, financial institution, or approved charitable institution.
Purpose must be higher education of self, spouse, children, or a student for whom assessee is legal guardian.
Higher education means any recognized course after Class XII or senior secondary.
Deduction is available for the initial year and up to 7 succeeding tax years (total 8 years).
There is no monetary ceiling on the interest amount deductible; principal repayment gets no deduction.

flow.title: Eligibility for Education Loan Deduction
steps: Verify loan is from recognized FI or charity
Ensure education is post-senior secondary
Confirm student is self, spouse, or child
Check 8-year time limit from initial year
Deduct 100% of interest paid without limit

topics.example: If Mr. B pays ₹48,000 interest and ₹2,20,000 principal on education loans taken for himself and his children, only the ₹48,000 interest is deductible.
remember: Deduction is available for 8 consecutive years or until interest is fully paid.
No deduction is allowed for principal repayment.
mistakes: Attempting to claim deduction for interest on loans taken from relatives or employers.

quiz.q: What is the maximum monetary ceiling on interest deduction under section 129?
quiz.why: Section 129 allows the entire interest paid without any upper monetary cap for up to 8 years.

quiz.q: For how many continuous tax years can an individual claim deduction under section 129?
o: Till loan is fully repaid even if 15 years
quiz.why: Deduction is available for the initial year plus 7 immediately succeeding years, i.e., 8 tax years.

topics.title: Interest on Loans for Residential House Property
explain: Both sections provide extra interest deduction over and above section 22 limit under optional regime.
Section 130: Loan sanctioned in T.Y. 2016-17; loan ≤ ₹35 lakhs; house value ≤ ₹50 lakhs; max ₹50,000.
Section 131: Loan sanctioned between 01.04.2019 and 31.03.2022; stamp duty value ≤ ₹45 lakhs; max ₹1,50,000.
Assessee must be a first-time home buyer not owning any residential house on sanction date.
Loans must be taken from a bank or Housing Finance Company (HFC).
Neither deduction is available under the default tax regime u/s 202(1).

flow.title: Housing Loan Interest Layering
steps: Claim up to ₹2,00,000 interest u/s 22(1)(b)
Check loan sanction period and property value
Verify assessee owned no other house property
Apply section 130 (max ₹50k) or 131 (max ₹1.5L)
Disallow duplicate claim across multiple sections

topics.example: Mr. A pays ₹3,87,000 interest on a loan sanctioned in 2021 for a ₹45 lakh house: ₹2,00,000 is deducted under house property, and ₹1,50,000 under section 131.
remember: Section 131 cap is ₹1,50,000; Section 130 cap is ₹50,000.
Cannot claim section 131 if eligible under section 130.
mistakes: Claiming section 131 when the loan was borrowed from a non-banking financial company (NBFC) that is not an HFC.

quiz.q: What is the maximum stamp duty value of a house to qualify for deduction under section 131?
quiz.why: Section 131 requires the stamp duty value of the residential house property not to exceed ₹45 lakhs.

quiz.q: What is the maximum deduction available under section 131 per tax year?
quiz.why: The maximum permissible deduction under section 131 is ₹1,50,000.

topics.title: Interest on Loan for Purchase of Electric Vehicle
explain: Available to individuals purchasing an electric vehicle for personal or business use.
Available only if the assessee opts out of the default tax regime.
Loan must be sanctioned by a bank or eligible NBFC between 01.04.2019 and 31.03.2023.
Maximum deduction allowed is interest payable up to ₹1,50,000 per tax year.
Benefit continues every year until the loan is fully repaid.
No deduction is allowed for the same interest under any other section.

flow.title: Testing Section 132 Deduction
steps: Check assessee status (individual only)
Verify loan sanctioned between 1.4.2019 and 31.3.2023
Ensure lender is bank or recognized NBFC
Determine annual interest payable
Cap deduction at lower of interest or ₹1,50,000

topics.example: Mr. C took an EV loan from an NBFC sanctioned on 01.04.2020. Annual interest is ₹2,00,000. He gets a deduction of ₹1,50,000 u/s 132.
remember: Loan sanction window: 1st April 2019 to 31st March 2023.
Deduction limit: ₹1,50,000 per year.
mistakes: Claiming deduction for loans sanctioned before 01.04.2019 or after 31.03.2023.

quiz.q: Mr. D was sanctioned an electric vehicle loan on 30.03.2019. How much deduction can he claim u/s 132?
quiz.why: The loan was sanctioned before 01.04.2019, making it ineligible for section 132 deduction.

quiz.q: What is the maximum yearly deduction allowed under section 132?
quiz.why: Section 132 restricts the maximum interest deduction to ₹1,50,000 per tax year.

topics.title: Donations to Certain Funds and Charitable Institutions
explain: Available to assessees paying tax under the optional/normal tax regime.
Four categories: 100% without limit, 50% without limit, 100% with limit, 50% with limit.
No limit 100%: PM CARES, National Defence Fund, Swachh Bharat Kosh, Clean Ganga Fund.
Qualifying limit: 10% of Adjusted GTI (GTI less capital gains, other deductions except 133).
Qualifying limit pool covers family planning (100%) and approved charities/temples (50%).
No deduction allowed for donations exceeding ₹2,000 made in cash.

flow.title: Computing Section 133 Qualifying Limit
steps: Calculate Adjusted Gross Total Income
Compute Qualifying Limit as 10% of Adjusted GTI
Allocate limit first to 100% limited donations
Allocate remaining limit to 50% limited donations
Sum all 4 categories to find total deduction

topics.example: If adjusted GTI is ₹6,00,000, 10% limit is ₹60,000. Donating ₹40,000 to family planning (100%) leaves ₹20,000 for a charitable trust, giving 50% of ₹20,000 = ₹10,000.
remember: Cash donations exceeding ₹2,000 are not eligible for any deduction.
Qualifying limit is always 10% of adjusted GTI.
mistakes: Including donations in kind (like clothes or food); deduction is allowed ONLY for sums of money.

quiz.q: An assessee makes a cash donation of ₹5,000 to an approved charitable institution. What deduction is allowed u/s 133?
quiz.why: Any donation exceeding ₹2,000 paid in cash is completely disallowed under section 133(5).

quiz.q: Which of the following donations qualifies for 100% deduction without any qualifying limit?
quiz.why: PM CARES Fund falls under Category I: 100% deduction without any qualifying limit.

topics.title: Deduction in Respect of Rent Paid
explain: Available to individuals who do not receive any House Rent Allowance (HRA).
Assessee, spouse, minor child, or HUF must not own residential accommodation at that place.
Deduction is the least of three limits: ₹5,000 per month.
Second limit: Actual rent paid minus 10% of total income.
Third limit: 25% of total income (before this deduction).
Total income for this section is computed after all other Chapter VIII deductions.

flow.title: Section 134 Least of Three Rule
steps: Calculate Limit 1: Actual rent minus 10% total income
Calculate Limit 2: 25% of total income
Calculate Limit 3: Statutory cap of ₹5,000 per month
Compare all three computed figures
Select the lowest figure as deduction

remember: Statutory ceiling is ₹5,000 per month (₹60,000/year).
Cannot be claimed if assessee gets HRA from employer.
mistakes: Claiming section 134 deduction when owning a house at the place where the assessee resides or works.

quiz.q: What is the absolute maximum annual deduction permitted under section 134?
quiz.why: The statutory cap is ₹5,000 per month, which equals ₹60,000 in a full year.

quiz.q: Can an employee receiving House Rent Allowance (HRA) claim deduction under section 134?
quiz.why: Section 134 is only available to assessees who do not receive tax-exempt HRA.

topics.title: Donations for Scientific Research and Political Contributions
explain: Section 135: 100% deduction for donations to scientific research associations for non-business assessees.
Cash donations exceeding ₹2,000 are disallowed u/s 135.
Section 136: 100% deduction to Indian companies for contributions to political parties or electoral trusts.
Company advertisements in political party souvenirs/brochures qualify as contributions u/s 136.
Section 137: 100% deduction to any other person for political contributions.
Under sections 136 and 137, cash contributions are strictly 100% disallowed.

flow.title: Political Contribution Testing
steps: Identify donor category (Company: 136, Others: 137)
Confirm recipient is registered party or trust
Verify payment mode (cheque, draft, ECS)
If cash paid, deduction is strictly zero
Allow 100% of non-cash payment as deduction

topics.example: ABC Ltd. donates ₹2,00,000 by cheque to an electoral trust and ₹25,000 for an advertisement in a party brochure. Total deduction u/s 136 is ₹2,25,000.
remember: Zero deduction if political contribution is made in cash.
Individual claiming u/s 137 must opt out of the default tax regime.
mistakes: Claiming deduction under section 137 for advertisements in party brochures (only companies get this u/s 136).

quiz.q: Mr. Rohan donates ₹1,50,000 by cheque to an electoral trust and pays ₹25,000 for a political brochure ad. Under section 137, deduction is:
quiz.why: Only companies can claim brochure advertisements (u/s 136). Individuals u/s 137 only get direct contributions (₹1,50,000).

quiz.q: What is the maximum cash contribution allowed for deduction to political parties under section 136/137?
quiz.why: No deduction is allowed under section 136 or 137 for any sum contributed in cash.

topics.title: Special Provisions for SEZ Units
explain: Provides export profit deduction for units established in Special Economic Zones.
Requires approval on or before 31.03.2020 and operations commencing within specified timelines.
First 5 years: 100% of export profits.
Next 5 years (Years 6-10): 50% of export profits.
Next 5 years (Years 11-15): 50% of export profits subject to SEZ Re-investment Reserve creation.
Profits = Profits of unit × (Export Turnover / Total Turnover); must file return within due date.

flow.title: SEZ Deduction Phasing
steps: Years 1 to 5: 100% of export profits
Years 6 to 10: 50% of export profits
Years 11 to 15: 50% if credited to reserve
Acquire plant & machinery within 3 years
Misuse of reserve deemed taxable profits

topics.example: A unit in Year 8 with ₹60 lakhs SEZ profits, ₹300 lakhs foreign export turnover, and ₹400 lakhs total turnover gets: 60 × (300/400) × 50% = ₹22.50 lakhs.
remember: Export proceeds must be brought into India in convertible foreign exchange within 6 months.
Audit report must be filed one month prior to return filing due date.
mistakes: Including freight, telecommunications, or insurance in export turnover when calculating the ratio.

quiz.q: What percentage of export profit is deductible under section 144 in the 8th year of operations?
quiz.why: Years 6 to 10 qualify for a 50% deduction of export profits.

quiz.q: In the case of amalgamation during the tax year, who can claim section 144 deduction for that year?
quiz.why: Section 144(8) explicitly bars the amalgamating unit and allows deduction to the amalgamated company.

topics.title: Deduction for Additional Employee Cost
explain: Available to an assessee subject to tax audit whose GTI includes business profits.
Available under both default and optional tax regimes.
Deduction is 30% of additional employee cost for 3 consecutive tax years.
Employee must be employed for at least 240 days (150 days for footwear/apparel/leather industry).
Emoluments must not exceed ₹25,000 per month.
Emoluments must be paid via banking/electronic channels, not in cash.

flow.title: Validating Additional Employee
steps: Check net employee count increases over last year
Verify monthly pay does not exceed ₹25,000
Ensure worked ≥ 240 days (150 for apparel)
Confirm employee participates in recognized PF
Allow 30% of eligible cost for 3 years

topics.example: If 75 qualifying new employees are hired on 1.4.2026 at ₹24,000/month, cost is ₹2,16,00,000. Deduction is 30% = ₹64,80,000 each year for 3 years.
remember: Monthly salary ceiling is ₹25,000.
Deduction is 30% per year for 3 consecutive tax years.
mistakes: Treating casual employees not participating in recognized provident fund as additional employees.

quiz.q: What is the qualifying minimum period of employment during the tax year for footwear manufacturing workers u/s 146?
quiz.why: For apparel, footwear, and leather industries, the minimum employment period is relaxed to 150 days.

quiz.q: Is deduction under section 146 available to an assessee paying tax under the default tax regime u/s 202(1)?
quiz.why: Section 146 is one of the specific business deductions permitted even under the default tax regime.

topics.title: Royalty Income of Authors and Patent Holders
explain: Available to resident individuals under the optional tax regime.
Section 151 covers book authors of literary, artistic, or scientific works (not textbooks/guides).
Section 151 deduction: Lower of eligible royalty or ₹3,00,000; non-lump sum royalty capped at 15% of book value.
Section 152 covers patentee inventors registered under the Patents Act, 1970.
Section 152 deduction: Whole of royalty or ₹3,00,000, whichever is less.
Foreign royalty earnings must be repatriated into India within 6 months in convertible foreign exchange.

flow.title: Determining Royalty Deduction
steps: Confirm assessee is resident author or patentee
If non-lumpsum book royalty, cap at 15% book sales
Deduct attributable expenses to find net royalty
Limit to foreign exchange repatriated in 6 months
Cap deduction at statutory limit of ₹3,00,000

topics.example: An author earns ₹2,88,000 abroad at 18% royalty. Capped at 15% gives ₹2,40,000. If ₹2,30,000 is repatriated and expenses are ₹40,000, deduction u/s 151 is ₹1,90,000.
remember: Maximum deduction under both section 151 and 152 is ₹3,00,000.
Section 151 does not apply to school textbooks, diaries, or magazines.
mistakes: Claiming section 152 deduction on sale proceeds of patented commercial products rather than patent royalties.

quiz.q: What is the maximum royalty rate allowable on book value for section 151 deduction if not received in lump sum?
quiz.why: Non-lump sum royalty is restricted to a maximum of 15% of the value of books sold.

quiz.q: Mr. R earned ₹5,00,000 from sale of products manufactured using his patented process. What is his deduction u/s 152?
quiz.why: Section 152 covers royalty for patent usage, not consideration from sale of manufactured products.

topics.title: Interest on Deposits & Persons with Disability
explain: Both sections are available only under the optional tax regime.
Section 153: Non-senior citizens/HUF get up to ₹10,000 deduction on savings account interest.
Section 153: Senior citizens get up to ₹50,000 deduction on ALL deposits (savings + fixed/recurring).
Section 154: Deduction directly to a resident individual who is a person with disability.
Ordinary disability (40% to 79%) receives a flat deduction of ₹75,000.
Severe disability (80% or more) receives an enhanced flat deduction of ₹1,25,000.

flow.title: Applying Sections 153 & 154
steps: For interest, check age (below 60 vs senior citizen)
Non-seniors: Max ₹10,000 on savings deposits only
Senior citizens: Max ₹50,000 on all bank/post office deposits
For self-disability, obtain medical certificate
Deduct flat ₹75,000 (disability) or ₹1,25,000 (severe)

topics.example: A 65-year-old earns ₹55,000 fixed deposit interest. He claims ₹50,000 u/s 153. A person with 85% disability claims a flat ₹1,25,000 u/s 154.
remember: Senior citizens can claim FD and savings interest up to ₹50,000 u/s 153.
Section 154 is for the disabled assessee themselves; Section 127 is for dependant disability.
mistakes: Allowing fixed deposit interest deduction under section 153 to non-senior citizens.

quiz.q: What is the maximum deduction allowed u/s 153 on fixed deposit interest for a 62-year-old resident individual?
quiz.why: Senior citizens are allowed up to ₹50,000 deduction on all deposits including fixed deposits.

quiz.q: What is the flat deduction under section 154 for an individual suffering from severe disability (85%)?
quiz.why: Section 154 provides a flat deduction of ₹1,25,000 in cases of severe disability (80% or more).
